description: Why: the standard Rust convention for option-as-result is Some(value) means something was found / returned; None means absent / nothing to act on. Using None to mean 'allowed' and Some(result) to mean 'rejected' is the inverse of the expected convention and surprises readers of check_and_consume call sites. What: rate_limit.rs PeerRateLimiter::check and TokenBucket::check_and_consume return None for allow and Some(RateLimitResult::Exhausted) for reject. Rename to return a bool or an explicit enum like RateLimitDecision::Allow / RateLimitDecision::Deny(action).
title: Rate limiter inverted Option semantics: None means allowed, Some means rejected
